memory_candidates.content: When a Batch Gate Deferral directive asks you to discharge a redeploy/full-verification phase against a scoped narrowing invocation while siblings are concurrently running their own verify-deploy.sh on the same shared tree, a full unscoped sweep run anyway (for visibility) can show spurious gate timeouts (e.g. a 60s-budgeted gate exceeding its limit) purely from resource contention -- confirmed by re-running that gate's underlying check in isolation (e.g. validate-state.sh --deep directly) and seeing it pass well within budget. Before treating any full-sweep failure as a real regression, check git log/git status on the specific flagged file(s): a finding outside this task's own file_scope with no related commit from this dispatch is very likely pre-existing drift or contention noise, not something this task caused.
